text.p: IKON Office Solutions Inc said it was accelerating its program to transform itself into a streamlined and integrated provider of total office solutions.
IKON also said it plans to announce transformation expenses on a quarterly basis so that these costs can be easily tracked relative to the growth of the business.
IKON will begin reporting the expenses separately beginning with the fiscal second quarter ending March 31.
It said it would complete the transformation program in October 1998, more than a year ahead of schedule.
Total transformation costs are not expected to increase, the company said in a statement released Thursday.

The most significant component of the transformation expenses in the second quarter will be the write-off of the capital costs from the SAP computer platform pilot project, it said. IKON said it had decided to base its information technology platform on the common platform that 75 percent of its operations currently use.

Announced in early 1996, the transformation is part of IKON's strategy to move from what was more than 80 individually operating copier dealers with total revenues of about $3 billion, to an integrated $10 billion company by the year 2000, providing total office technology solutions ranging from copiers, digital printers and document-management services to systems integration, training and other networking technology services.
